name: IBM Fez routing and calibrated noise for full and 75% pruned QAOA
initial_layout: logical bit i maps to fixed selected physical patch position i; identical for all methods
scheduling: ALAP, explicit padded idle delays, final barrier; native rz/sx/x/cz/id basis
noise_cohort: Union of every Babai-nonoptimal case and a fixed random 32-case subset. The 441 Babai-optimal hybrid outputs are deterministic, so their noisy simulation is unnecessary for full-cohort hybrid statistics. Reference-based computational shortcut only: no oracle is supplied to a solver and no runtime advantage is claimed from skipping these cases.
noise_model: Aer calibrated native gate depolarization plus gate-time T1/T2 relaxation, explicit T1/T2 relaxation on scheduled idle delays, and asymmetric readout confusion from the same live public calibration. Zero temperature; ideal initial reset. No crosstalk, leakage, drift, coherent calibration errors, mitigation, twirling, dynamical decoupling or refitting.
analysis: Estimate mixed-state probabilities by averaging 64 independently sampled noise trajectories; apply readout analytically to each trajectory. These are Monte Carlo estimates, not exact noisy probabilities or hardware shots. Store low-cost probability masses per trajectory and full mean distributions. Keep fixed-cohort Monte Carlo intervals separate from paired group-bootstrap intervals. Main outcomes: mean extra hybrid distance improvement over Babai, paired differences versus full, gate counts and scheduled duration. Both pruned variants remain fixed; no adaptive selection or stopping by quality.

planning.note: Only local time estimates with default repetition delay and reset duration. Not guaranteed quota usage, not permission to submit, and actual available account balance remains unverified.

limitations: One currently accessible IBM device, one calibration snapshot, one connected 16-qubit patch and one fixed routing seed. Not a claim about every IBM processor or placement.
Calibration-based Markovian noise is an approximation, not an experiment on the device. Calibration drift, crosstalk, leakage and coherent errors are excluded.
64 noise trajectories per circuit give Monte Carlo uncertainty; displayed best-of-shot results are nonlinear plug-in estimates with a finite-trajectory bias check, not exact predictions.
All 512 examples contribute to hybrid metrics. QAOA-only noisy population summaries use only the separate random 32-case subset, never the enriched union.
No new fitting; this is a follow-up on the existing fresh-validation cohort. Any new changes motivated by these outcomes need new evaluation.
Fewer native gates need not translate proportionally into QPU usage because readout, reset, repetition delay and job overhead also consume time.
Small Module-LWE parameters, no secure ML-KEM attack, no end-to-end quantum advantage, and no real QPU execution.
